subject.title: fix(agents): strip MiniMax stream-boundary marker from transport payload text

question: Should the MiniMax marker fix follow the provider-scoped, terminal-only approach in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105243 rather than adding global deletion rules to shared transport sanitization?
rationale: The safe ownership boundary determines whether ordinary content from every provider can be altered; the current branch and the related PR embody incompatible approaches.

options.title: Adopt provider-scoped cleanup
options.body: Move the MiniMax repair into the MiniMax provider stream path, preserve literal marker-like content, and submit the unrelated UI fixes separately.

options.title: Keep shared sanitization
options.body: Accept global stripping only with explicit maintainer approval plus regression proof that non-MiniMax and literal marker-like payloads remain intact.

options.title: Pause the marker portion
options.body: Do not merge the shared sanitizer while the existing provider-scoped PR is the active candidate for the same user-visible problem.

recommendation.title: Adopt provider-scoped cleanup
recommendation.body: Move the MiniMax repair into the MiniMax provider stream path, preserve literal marker-like content, and submit the unrelated UI fixes separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Their active overlapping implementation provides the most direct evidence about the provider-specific boundary and stream contract.
